subject: Agriculture
title: Hydroponics and Aeroponics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hydroponics and Aeroponics.

hook.text: In hydroponics, plants grow with roots dangling in water. In aeroponics, roots hang in air and get misted with nutrients.

buildup.text: Soil is just a medium—plants need water, nutrients, and support. Remove the soil and you control everything.

discovery.text: Hydroponic lettuce grows 30–50% faster than soil-grown because roots access nutrients directly without soil resistance.

twist.text: NASA studied aeroponics for growing food in space. Mars colonists may eat aeroponic potatoes before Earth farmers do.

climax.text: Aquaponics combines fish farming with hydroponics—fish waste feeds plants, plants filter water for fish.

punchline.text: Plants don't need soil. That's 10,000 years of agriculture overturned.

quiz.question: What is aquaponics?
options: Combining fish farming with hydroponics—fish waste feeds plants, plants filter water
